categories.title: Email openings
categories.description: Greetings and first lines that set the right tone for the reader.

phrases.phrase: Dear Ms. / Mr. [Last name],
phrases.meaning: Standard greeting for a formal email when you know the person's name.
phrases.example: Dear Ms. Okafor, I am writing about the renovation work in unit 504.

phrases.phrase: To whom it may concern,
phrases.meaning: Formal greeting when you don't know who will read the email; use sparingly.
phrases.example: To whom it may concern, I would like to report a billing error on my account.

phrases.phrase: I hope this email finds you well.
phrases.meaning: Polite warm-up line before getting to the point, for semi-formal emails.
phrases.example: I hope this email finds you well. I wanted to follow up on our conversation last week.

phrases.phrase: Hi [first name], it's been ages!
phrases.meaning: Friendly opening for a friend you haven't contacted in a while.
phrases.example: Hi Daniel, it's been ages! I was so happy to hear about your new job.

phrases.phrase: Thank you for your quick reply.
phrases.meaning: Opening line when answering someone who has already written to you.
phrases.example: Thank you for your quick reply. I have a few more questions about the course.

phrases.phrase: My name is … and I am a resident of …
phrases.meaning: Introduces yourself when the reader doesn't know you.
phrases.example: My name is Arjun Mehta, and I am a resident of unit 404 in your building.

phrases.phrase: I hope you and your family are doing well.
phrases.meaning: Warm opening for a neighbour, friend or colleague you know personally.
phrases.example: Hi Priya, I hope you and your family are doing well after the storm.

phrases.phrase: I am contacting you on behalf of …
phrases.meaning: Shows you are writing for someone else or for a group.
phrases.example: I am contacting you on behalf of the parents' committee at Maple Elementary.

categories.title: Stating the purpose
categories.description: Say clearly, in the first paragraph, why you are writing.

phrases.phrase: I am writing to …
phrases.meaning: The clearest way to state the purpose of a formal email.
phrases.example: I am writing to request a refund for the cancelled course.

phrases.phrase: I am writing with regard to …
phrases.meaning: Formal way to name the topic of your email.
phrases.example: I am writing with regard to the order I placed on March 3.

phrases.phrase: The reason I'm writing is that …
phrases.meaning: Slightly less formal way to introduce your purpose.
phrases.example: The reason I'm writing is that my delivery arrived damaged.

phrases.phrase: I wanted to let you know that …
phrases.meaning: Introduces news or information in a friendly way.
phrases.example: I wanted to let you know that I'll be in town next month.

phrases.phrase: I would like to bring to your attention …
phrases.meaning: Politely raises a problem with someone responsible.
phrases.example: I would like to bring to your attention a safety issue in the parking garage.

phrases.phrase: I'm just writing to say thanks for …
phrases.meaning: Casual opening for a thank-you email.
phrases.example: I'm just writing to say thanks for looking after our house during the storm.

phrases.phrase: Following our phone conversation on …,
phrases.meaning: Connects the email to an earlier conversation.
phrases.example: Following our phone conversation on Tuesday, I am sending the documents you requested.

phrases.phrase: I am reaching out to ask whether …
phrases.meaning: Introduces a question or a request politely.
phrases.example: I am reaching out to ask whether the program will be offered again this fall.

categories.title: Complaining politely
categories.description: Describe a problem firmly but courteously, and explain its impact.

phrases.phrase: I was disappointed to find that …
phrases.meaning: Expresses dissatisfaction without sounding aggressive.
phrases.example: I was disappointed to find that the table had a deep crack in it.

phrases.phrase: Unfortunately, …
phrases.meaning: Softens the start of a sentence that reports a problem.
phrases.example: Unfortunately, the work often starts before 7 a.m., even on weekends.

phrases.phrase: This has caused me considerable inconvenience.
phrases.meaning: States the impact of the problem formally.
phrases.example: This has caused me considerable inconvenience, as I had to take a day off work.

phrases.phrase: To make matters worse, …
phrases.meaning: Adds a second, more serious part of the problem.
phrases.example: To make matters worse, nobody from the centre has contacted me since.

phrases.phrase: I'm sure you will agree that this is not acceptable.
phrases.meaning: Firmly invites the reader to see your side.
phrases.example: I'm sure you will agree that a week-long delay without notice is not acceptable.

phrases.phrase: It has been going on for …
phrases.meaning: Shows how long a problem has lasted.
phrases.example: It has been going on for three weeks, and it is affecting my sleep.

phrases.phrase: As a long-standing customer, …
phrases.meaning: Reminds the company of your loyalty to strengthen a complaint.
phrases.example: As a long-standing customer, I expected a much better level of service.

phrases.phrase: I would appreciate it if this could be resolved by …
phrases.meaning: Sets a polite deadline for a solution.
phrases.example: I would appreciate it if this could be resolved by the end of the month.

categories.title: Making requests and suggestions
categories.description: Ask for action and propose solutions in a constructive way.

phrases.phrase: Would it be possible to …?
phrases.meaning: Polite, indirect way to ask for something.
phrases.example: Would it be possible to schedule the noisy work after 9 a.m.?

phrases.phrase: I would be grateful if you could …
phrases.meaning: Very polite formal request.
phrases.example: I would be grateful if you could send a replacement chair as soon as possible.

phrases.phrase: One solution might be to …
phrases.meaning: Introduces a suggestion without sounding demanding.
phrases.example: One solution might be to post the work schedule in the lobby.

phrases.phrase: Could you possibly …?
phrases.meaning: Softened request for a favour.
phrases.example: Could you possibly water my plants while I'm away?

phrases.phrase: Why don't you …?
phrases.meaning: Friendly suggestion to someone you know well.
phrases.example: Why don't you look at apartments near the subway line?

phrases.phrase: It might be a good idea to …
phrases.meaning: Gentle advice or suggestion.
phrases.example: It might be a good idea to visit the neighbourhood on a weekday evening.

phrases.phrase: I would suggest that …
phrases.meaning: Formal suggestion; often followed by a base-form verb.
phrases.example: I would suggest that the contractor clean the hallway at the end of each day.

phrases.phrase: If you don't mind, I'd like to …
phrases.meaning: Asks permission politely before proposing something.
phrases.example: If you don't mind, I'd like to take you out for dinner next weekend.

phrases.phrase: Please let me know whether …
phrases.meaning: Asks for a decision or confirmation.
phrases.example: Please let me know whether you can approve my leave by Friday.

categories.title: Closing an email
categories.description: End with a clear next step and a sign-off that matches the opening.

phrases.phrase: I look forward to hearing from you.
phrases.meaning: Standard formal closing line that invites a reply.
phrases.example: I look forward to hearing from you at your earliest convenience.

phrases.phrase: Thank you for your time and attention.
phrases.meaning: Formal thanks before signing off.
phrases.example: Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

phrases.phrase: Please do not hesitate to contact me if …
phrases.meaning: Offers further information.
phrases.example: Please do not hesitate to contact me if you need any further details.

phrases.phrase: Sincerely, / Best regards,
phrases.meaning: Sign-offs for formal and semi-formal emails.
phrases.example: Best regards, Arjun Mehta

phrases.phrase: Can't wait to see you!
phrases.meaning: Enthusiastic closing for a friend.
phrases.example: Let me know your flight details. Can't wait to see you!

phrases.phrase: Thanks again for everything.
phrases.meaning: Warm closing for a thank-you email.
phrases.example: Thanks again for everything you did for us last weekend.

phrases.phrase: Take care, / Cheers,
phrases.meaning: Friendly sign-offs for people you know well.
phrases.example: Take care, and say hi to your family for me.

phrases.phrase: I trust this matter will be resolved promptly.
phrases.meaning: Firm, formal closing for a complaint.
phrases.example: I trust this matter will be resolved promptly, and I thank you in advance.

categories.title: Opinions, reasons and concessions
categories.description: For survey responses and opinion tasks: state a position, support it, and acknowledge the other side.

phrases.phrase: In my view, … is the better option because …
phrases.meaning: Clearly states your choice and links it to a reason.
phrases.example: In my view, Option B is the better option because it helps more residents.

phrases.phrase: The main reason I prefer … is that …
phrases.meaning: Introduces your strongest argument.
phrases.example: The main reason I prefer the hybrid week is that it saves commuting time.

phrases.phrase: Another advantage is that …
phrases.meaning: Adds a second supporting point.
phrases.example: Another advantage is that the library would serve people of all ages.

phrases.phrase: Admittedly, …; however, …
phrases.meaning: Concedes a point to the other side, then returns to your argument.
phrases.example: Admittedly, a sports complex is popular; however, it would benefit fewer people.

phrases.phrase: While some people argue that …, I believe …
phrases.meaning: Contrasts an opposing view with your own.
phrases.example: While some people argue that phones distract students, I believe they can be useful tools.

phrases.phrase: For example, …
phrases.meaning: Introduces a concrete example to support a point.
phrases.example: For example, my neighbour's children study at the library every evening.

phrases.phrase: As a result, …
phrases.meaning: Shows a consequence.
phrases.example: As a result, more people would take the bus instead of driving.

phrases.phrase: Overall, I am convinced that …
phrases.meaning: Sums up your position at the end.
phrases.example: Overall, I am convinced that free transit would benefit the whole city.

phrases.phrase: It's true that …, but …
phrases.meaning: Less formal concession.
phrases.example: It's true that the garden would cost money, but it would bring neighbours together.

categories.title: Speaking: fillers and transitions
categories.description: Natural ways to buy time, organize your answer and move between ideas when speaking.

phrases.phrase: That's a good question. Let me think…
phrases.meaning: Buys a second or two naturally instead of a silent pause.
phrases.example: That's a good question. Let me think… I'd say the most important thing is to make a budget.

phrases.phrase: First of all, … / On top of that, …
phrases.meaning: Signposts the order of your ideas.
phrases.example: First of all, you should track your spending. On top of that, try cooking at home more.

phrases.phrase: In the picture, I can see …
phrases.meaning: Opens a scene description.
phrases.example: In the picture, I can see a busy skating rink in a park.

phrases.phrase: In the background / in the foreground / on the left, …
phrases.meaning: Locates details in a picture for a listener who can't see it.
phrases.example: In the background, there are some snow-covered pine trees.

phrases.phrase: It looks like … is about to …
phrases.meaning: Makes a prediction based on the picture.
phrases.example: It looks like the little girl is about to fall.

phrases.phrase: I'm pretty sure that … / Chances are that …
phrases.meaning: Expresses a likely prediction with confidence.
phrases.example: Chances are that the man will have to pay an extra baggage fee.

phrases.phrase: What I mean is …
phrases.meaning: Rephrases or clarifies an idea after a slip.
phrases.example: What I mean is that you should save a little every month, even if it's only fifty dollars.

phrases.phrase: Think about it this way: …
phrases.meaning: Persuades by reframing the situation for the listener.
phrases.example: Think about it this way: the SUV costs more now, but it's much safer in winter.

phrases.phrase: So, to sum up, …
phrases.meaning: Signals that you are wrapping up before time runs out.
phrases.example: So, to sum up, I think talking to Kevin directly is the best choice.
